mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding 6 months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically below the median market return at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% signals contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces input demand and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months, or the median return is not statistically different from zero.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall in payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 1 standard deviation within the same month signals a sharp labor market deterioration, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE up > 1σ AND PAYEMS down > 1σ in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 70% of triggered months, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant at 5% in a regression model.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening housing demand, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month averages signals a restrictive monetary policy in an inflationary environment, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 12-mo MA AND CPIAUCSL > 12-mo MA in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered months, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant at 5% in a regression model.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized growth in real personal income (proxied by the sum of GDPC1 and PAYEMS growth) above 4% for three consecutive quarters signals an expansionary demand shock, which boosts corporate earnings and predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: Annualized growth in (GDPC1+PAYEMS) > 4% for 3 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive in at least 70% of triggered quarters, or the interaction effect is not significant at 5% in a regression model.
